v1 92.706/93.061. THE FILTER NEVER OPENS: modern deep house, 118 -> 118.5 bpm, A minor.
- The chord stab lives inside a BARBER-POLE FILTER: four copies band-passed an octave apart, carried up an octave every eight bars by one song-time sawtooth, while the lowest fades in and the highest fades out. At each wrap every copy lands where its neighbour was, so the filter keeps opening and never gets brighter.
- The stair (A B C E) answers t1 as the stab's top note, chopped off the beat.
- Machine-kit rumble kick, hats, claps, a 3-3-2 rim; a rolling bass, pumped.
- Mini-drops with a noise rise. A fader ride lets the break and the drops sit lower.
- SEAMS: in, t1's outro (kick, hats, phantom bass, the Shepard stair at 118) plays over t2's first 16 bars of kick and hats, the pole entering at bar 9. Out, t2's last 16 bars at 118.5 keep kick, hats and the pole on an open A-E fifth over t3's Em head (mixplan updated).
-11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (A moving progression under the pole was tried: it split the grooves into shards; reverted.) (Not queued.)
next: Distinctness from t1 (same key and tempo by design).

note: v2 93.138/93.414 (v1 rescored 93.15; kept on judgment: chirper-one's note). THE POLE TURNS ROUND (T2_R2). For the eight bars before the last groove (B1's last four and the drop), the stab moves to a second barber pole running DOWN: four copies at 400-3200 Hz, carried down an octave every four bars, the highest fading in and the lowest out. Measured on the solo copy: its centre falls 725 -> 503 Hz, twice. B2 turns the pole back up, so the endless opening is felt by contrast. Seams unchanged (t1>t2 1.7 dB, t2>t3 2.8 dB sub range, swap mid). -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)
